question.problem: Given that the random variable $Y∼\text{Exp}(\frac{4}{3}),$ calculate $P(Y\ge 2).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $Y$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda y}, & y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
Y∼\text{Exp}(\frac{4}{3}).
$$

So, $Y$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}{e}^{-4y/3}, & y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(Y\ge 2)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 2) & ={\int }_{2}^{\infty }f(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{\infty }\frac{4}{3}{e}^{-4y/3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{{e}^{-4y/3}|}_{2}^{\infty } \\  & ={e}^{-8/3} \\  & ≈0.0695\end{aligned}
$$
